Chapter 10: Inspiring Others to Become “Freds”
You know, one of the most powerful things about the mail carrier’s story is how it sparks something in others. When you see someone who really goes above and beyond, it makes you pause and think—could I do that too? Turns out, this kind of effort is contagious. It spreads from person to person, from small groups to whole communities. Before you know it, everyone’s raising the bar.
Let me share a quick example. There was this small business owner who, honestly, was struggling just to keep the doors open. Instead of giving up, they decided to follow the mail carrier’s lead. They started by training their team to greet every customer with real warmth, to remember folks’ names and little preferences, and to look for ways to surprise and delight. At first, it wasn’t easy—getting everyone excited about these changes took some work. But as customers started noticing and responding, something shifted. The staff began to take genuine pride in what they did. Pretty soon, employees were coming up with their own creative ways to add value. And guess what? The business started thriving.
What became really clear is that leadership isn’t about barking orders or handing out to-do lists. It’s about leading by example. Most of us don’t realize just how much influence we actually have, but when you show others what’s possible through your own actions, it inspires them to step up too.
It’s easy to fall into the trap of thinking change always has to start at the top, or that one person can’t really make a difference. But here’s something to remember: every act of service, every moment where you genuinely care, it sets a new standard. When people witness that, they’re a whole lot more likely to try it for themselves.
The mail carrier’s story is a powerful reminder that inspiration might just be the greatest gift you can offer. By choosing to be a “Fred,” you’re opening the door for others to do the same—and that ripple effect can transform families, workplaces, even entire communities.
So here’s the key: don’t wait for someone else to take the lead. Start right where you are. Let your example light the way and see how many others decide to join you.
